μοιχαλίς, -ίδος, ἡ
(= Att.. μοιχάς, fem. of μοιχός), [in LXX: Pro.18.22 30:20), Ezk.16.38; 23.45, Hos.3.1, Mal.3.5 (נַאֲפוּף, נָאַף) * ;] 
an adulteress: Rom.7.3 meton., for μοιχεία, 2Pe.2.14. Metaphorical, of infidelity to God (cf. Ezk.16.15 ff. Ezk.23.43 ff., al.), Jas.4.4; as an adj., Mat.12.39; 16.4, Mrk.8.8.†
(AS)

(ἀντλέω), 
__(a) prop., what is drawn (Diosc.); 
__(b) a vessel to draw with, a bucket (Plut.; see Abbott, Essays, 88): Jhn.4.11.†
(AS)

οἰκοδομή, -ῆς, ἡ
(οἶκος, + δέμω, to build), [in LXX: 1Ch.29.1 A (בִּירָה), Ezk.17.17; 40.2 (בָּנָה, מִבְנֶה), Sir.22.16; 40.19, al. ;] 
= cl. οἰκοδομία (which see), -δόμησις (Thuc., Plat.), 
__1. the act of building; in NT always metaphorically, building up, edifying: Rom.14.19; 15.2, 1Co.14.26, 2Co.10.8; 13.10, Eph.4.29; with genitive obj., 1Co.14.12, 2Co.12.19, Eph.4.12, 16; λαλεῖν, λαβεῖν, οἰ., 1Co.14.3. 
__2. = οἰκοδόμημα, a building: Mat.24.1, Mrk.13.1-2; metaphorically, 1Co.3.9, 2Co.5.1, Eph.2.21.†
(AS)
